text: Cléo Hamon, born on 25 November 2001 in Cormeilles-en-Parisis, France, is a French pair skater. With her former partner Denys Strekalin, she is a two-time French national champion (2020, 2021), a 2018 Volvo Open Cup champion, and has competed in the final segment at three World Junior Championships (2017–2019). Her brother, Axel, is a triathlete. Hamon began learning to skate in 2006 and competed in ladies' singles, winning silver in the advanced novice category at the Rooster Cup in April 2016 and placing 13th at the Golden Bear of Zagreb in October 2016. In the 2014–2015 season, she partnered with Xavier Vauclin and became the French national novice champions in March 2015. She also skated with Brice Panizzi. In August 2016, Hamon teamed up with Ukraine's Denys Strekalin to compete for France in pairs, coached by Mehdi Bouzzine in Courbevoie. They made their international debut in February 2017, placing seventh in junior pairs at the Bavarian Open, and finished fourteenth at the 2017 World Junior Championships in Taipei, Taiwan. In September 2017, they debuted on the ISU Junior Grand Prix (JGP) series, placing eighth in Riga, Latvia. In December, they won silver at the French Championships behind Lola Esbrat / Andrei Novoselov. At the 2018 World Junior Championships in Sofia, Bulgaria, they finished eleventh. Competing in the 2018 JGP series, they placed sixth in Linz, Austria, and fifth in Ostrava, Czech Republic. They won gold at the Volvo Open Cup in November 2018. At the 2019 World Junior Championships in Zagreb, Croatia, they finished ninth. After placing eighth at the 2019 JGP United States, they debuted on the senior Challenger series with a seventh-place finish at the 2019 CS Finlandia Trophy, placing tenth at the 2019 CS Warsaw Cup, and ninth at their first European Championships. Hamon/Strekalin won the French senior national title for the first time due to the absence of James/Cipres and finished the season at the 2020 World Junior Championships, placing fifth. They were scheduled to participate in the 2020 World Championships in Montreal, which would have been their senior World debut, but the event was canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. With the pandemic ongoing, they began the new season at the 2020 CS Nebelhorn Trophy, where only pairs training in Europe competed; they were fourth after the short program and, after the top-ranked Hase/Seegert withdrew, placed third in the free and won the bronze medal. They were scheduled to make their Grand Prix debut at the 2020 Internationaux de France, but the event was canceled due to the pandemic. In February, they won their second straight National title. Later that month, they placed fifth at the International Challenge Cup. On March 1, they were named to the team for the 2021 World Championships, where they placed twentieth in their World Championship debut. They finished the season at the 2021 World Team Trophy, where they finished fifth in both segments and Team France finished in fifth place overall. They began the season at the 2021 Lombardia Trophy, where they finished in fourth place. They were originally scheduled to compete at the Nebelhorn Trophy, where the final Olympics spots would be decided, but were later replaced by Coline Keriven / Noël-Antoine Pierre. It was later announced that Hamon would be taking a break from figure skating due to health issues from burnout, which was the reason for their replacement at the Nebelhorn Trophy. The team later split, and Strekalin began looking for a new partner in October. (with Strekalin) GP: Grand Prix; CS: Challenger Series; JGP: Junior Grand Prix.
